java: GraphvizImageBuilder.isOpalisable initially requires non-strict UML, a NOTE entity, exactly one non-invisible incident link, and a non-note peer at lines 133-147 and 313-326.

GraphvizImageBuilder.buildImage performs an additional peer-node gate at lines 245-258: it calls Bibliotekon.getNode(peer) and marks the SvekEdge Opale only when that result is non-null. A container/group peer has no SvekNode, so its link remains ordinary.
SvekEdge.solve revokes the optimistic Opale flag when DotPath contains more than one cubic segment; SvekEdge.drawU suppresses the ordinary link group only while the final flag remains true.
EntityImageNote.drawU reverses the solved path toward the note, selects LEFT, RIGHT, UP, or DOWN by orthogonal distance in that tie order, and embeds the opposite endpoint as the leader tip.
rust: deployment_note_opale_connection at deployment.rs:6601-6642 checks strict UML, raw incident connection count, note peer kind, edge presence, and bezier_count, but it never rejects a declared container/group peer.

render_no_oracle collects every accepted connection index into opale_connection_indices, and render_no_oracle_edges returns early for those indices at deployment.rs:4559-4581 and 6353-6358. The missing group-peer gate therefore removes a real Java link event from paint.
The frozen binary's YAML for checker_group_peer_single_link retains one explicit GroupMemo-to-RackGroup connection, proving the failure is the Opale classifier rather than relation loss.

The frozen binary's YAML for checker_visible_plus_hidden_link omits the valid HiddenControlMemo -[hidden]- HiddenPeer relation entirely. That lost parser/layout/UID event changes Opale eligibility and downstream identity before the renderer classifier runs.

findings.summary: Rust wrongly marks a named note linked to a declared container as Opale.
findings.causal_evidence: Java's buildImage requires Bibliotekon.getNode(peer) to be non-null before handing an edge to EntityImageNote. A group peer has a Cluster rather than a SvekNode. Rust checks only whether the peer is another named note, then maps the group to a cluster endpoint proxy and suppresses the real relation.
findings.observable_divergence: Java: normal note plus visible lnk5. Rust: leader-bearing note and no link group.

findings.summary: A valid hidden relation is lost before Opale classification, changing layout/paint and downstream UID identity.
findings.causal_evidence: Java retains HiddenControlMemo -[hidden]- HiddenPeer as an invisible layout/link event. The frozen Rust YAML omits it, so deployment_note_opale_connection sees only one incident relation and the UID model never allocates the hidden link event.
findings.observable_divergence: Java paints visible lnk5 with a normal note and assigns AfterHidden ent0007; Rust absorbs the visible relation and assigns AfterHidden ent0006.

findings.summary: The positive controls support the implementation's central endpoint and side-selection model.
findings.evidence: Across source/destination, top-to-bottom/left-to-right, dotted/solid/directed, root/nested, labels/cardinalities, note-to-note, two-link, and strict-UML probes, Java and Rust agree on ordinary-link presence, Opale outline topology, side selection, and entity/link UID progression.
